title: Is This Your Umbrella?

lines.text: Good afternoon. Welcome to the lost property office. Can I help you?
Yes, please. I'm a student here. My friends and I can't find our things.
OK. What's your name?
My name's Diego Torres. I'm in Room twelve.
Right, Diego. Is this your umbrella? It's black.
No, it isn't. My umbrella is green. That black one is Marta's umbrella. Her name is on it.
Yes, you're right. What about this blue bag?
Yes! That's my bag. Thank you! And those are my brother's glasses. His glasses are always lost!
Ha! And this phone? Is it your sister's phone?
No, my sister's phone is pink. That's our teacher's phone. Her phone has a photo of her cat on it.
Great. Please take your bag, your brother's glasses and your teacher's phone.
Thanks a lot. Our teacher is very lucky today!

questions.explain_es: Diego dice: 'My umbrella is green.'
Diego dice: 'That black one is Marta's umbrella.'
Diego dice: 'Yes! That's my bag.'

questions.q: The phone is Diego's sister's phone.
questions.explain_es: Diego dice: 'my sister's phone is pink. That's our teacher's phone.'
Usamos 's para decir de quién es algo: 'my brother's glasses' (los lentes de mi hermano).
Diego dice: 'That's our teacher's phone.' El 's indica posesión.

questions.q: The teacher is a woman. Complete: '____ phone has a photo of her cat on it.'
questions.explain_es: Para una mujer usamos el posesivo 'her'. Diego dice: 'Her phone has a photo of her cat on it.'

dictation: Is this your umbrella?
My umbrella is green.

title: At the Language Exchange
focus: Present simple questions with do / does

lines.text: Hi! I'm Camilo. Is this your first time at the language exchange?
Yes, it is. I'm Hannah. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too. Where are you from?
I'm Australian. I'm from Perth. Where do you live, Camilo?
I live here in Bogotá, but my family is from Pasto. Do you speak Spanish?
Yes, a little. I study Spanish at a school near the university. Do you work or study?
I work in a hotel. I speak English with tourists every day. Does your school have classes on Saturdays?
No, it doesn't. It only has classes from Monday to Friday.
Oh, I see. And what about your friend there? Where does she come from?
That's Yuki. She's Japanese, from Osaka. She teaches English here.
Really? Does she like Colombian food?
Yes, she does! She loves arepas. Do you want to meet her?
Sure! Let's go and say hello.

questions.explain_es: Hannah dice: 'I'm Australian. I'm from Perth.'
Camilo dice: 'I work in a hotel.'

questions.q: Hannah's school has classes on Saturdays.
questions.explain_es: Hannah dice: 'No, it doesn't. It only has classes from Monday to Friday.'
Hannah dice: 'She teaches English here.'
Con 'you' la pregunta en presente simple empieza con 'Do': 'Do you speak Spanish?'
Con 'she' usamos 'does' en preguntas: 'Where does she come from?'

questions.q: Make a question: 'Yuki likes Colombian food.'
questions.explain_es: Pregunta con 'does' + verbo en forma base (like, sin -s). Camilo pregunta: 'Does she like Colombian food?'

dictation: Where do you live, Camilo?
I work in a hotel.

title: Shopping for a Picnic
focus: Countable and uncountable nouns with some / any

lines.text: Hi, Sam. I'm at the supermarket. What do we need for the picnic tomorrow?
Hi, Lucy. Let me look in the kitchen. We have some bread, but we don't have any cheese.
OK, I can buy some cheese. Do we have any tomatoes?
Yes, there are some tomatoes in the fridge. But there aren't any apples.
Right, some apples. What about drinks? Is there any orange juice?
No, there isn't any juice. Can you get some juice and some water, please?
Sure. Do you want any biscuits?
Yes, please! Get some chocolate biscuits. Oh, and we need some sugar for the lemonade.
Is there any milk for the coffee?
Yes, there's some milk. We don't need any milk.
OK. So, cheese, apples, juice, water, biscuits and sugar. Anything else?
No, that's all. Thanks, Lucy. See you soon!

questions.explain_es: Lucy dice: 'I'm at the supermarket.'
Sam dice: 'there are some tomatoes in the fridge.'

questions.q: Lucy needs to buy some milk.
questions.explain_es: Sam dice: 'there's some milk. We don't need any milk.'

questions.q: What do they need for the lemonade?
questions.explain_es: Sam dice: 'we need some sugar for the lemonade.'
En frases negativas usamos 'any': 'we don't have any cheese.'

questions.q: Can you get ____ juice and some water, please?
questions.explain_es: En peticiones y frases afirmativas usamos 'some': 'Can you get some juice and some water, please?'

questions.q: Find and correct the mistake: 'There aren't some apples.'
questions.explain_es: En negativo usamos 'any', no 'some'. Sam dice: 'there aren't any apples.'

dictation: We have some bread, but we don't have any cheese.
Is there any milk for the coffee?

title: First Day at the Office

lines.text: Hello! Are you the new designer?
Yes, I am. I'm Luis Herrera. I'm from Medellín.
Welcome, Luis! I'm Grace. I'm the office manager. Is this your first job?
No, it isn't. I'm twenty-eight, and this is my third job. But I'm a little nervous today.
Don't worry. We're very friendly here. This is your desk. It's next to the window.
Great! Who are they?
They're Tom and Priya. They're designers, too. Tom is from Canada and Priya is from India.
Are they nice?
Yes, they are. They're very funny. And that's our boss, Mr Chang. He isn't here on Mondays, but he's in the office today.
Is the kitchen on this floor?
No, it isn't. It's on the second floor. The coffee is free!
Perfect. I'm happy to be here.

Luis dice: 'No, it isn't. ... this is my third job.'

Mr Chang isn't here on Mondays

title: Life on a Coffee Farm

lines.text: Hello! My name's Gloria, and I live on a coffee farm near Jardín, in Antioquia.
I get up at five o'clock every day. First, I make coffee for my family, of course!
My husband, Jorge, feeds the chickens and the horse. Our son, Felipe, goes to school at seven.
At six thirty, I walk to the coffee plants with the workers. We pick the red coffee fruit by hand.
We work in the morning because the afternoon is very hot.
At twelve o'clock, we have lunch together. We eat beans, rice and plantain.
In the afternoon, Jorge dries the coffee in the sun, and I wash the clothes.
Felipe comes home at three. He helps his dad, and then he does his homework.
In the evening, we watch TV or listen to music. We don't go out much.
We go to bed at nine. Farm life is hard, but I love it!

questions.q: What time does Gloria get up?
questions.explain_es: Gloria dice: 'I get up at five o'clock every day.'
Gloria dice: 'Jorge feeds the chickens and the horse.'

questions.q: They pick coffee in the afternoon.
questions.explain_es: Gloria dice: 'We work in the morning because the afternoon is very hot.'
Gloria dice: 'Felipe comes home at three.'
Con 'he' el verbo 'go' cambia a 'goes': 'Felipe goes to school at seven.'

questions.q: Jorge ____ (dry) the coffee in the sun.
questions.explain_es: Consonante + y → -ies con 'he': dry → dries. 'Jorge dries the coffee in the sun.'

questions.q: Find and correct the mistake: 'Felipe help his dad.'
questions.explain_es: Con 'he' el verbo lleva -s: 'He helps his dad.'

dictation: We go to bed at nine.
We work in the morning because the afternoon is very hot.

title: The Gym Timetable

lines.text: Hi there! Welcome to FitZone. How can I help?
Hi. I want to join the gym. Can you tell me about the classes?
Sure. We usually have three classes every day. Spinning is always at seven in the morning.
Seven? That's early. I never get up before seven!
No problem. There's often a dance class at six in the evening. It's very popular.
Great. I sometimes go dancing with my friends. Is the gym busy at night?
It's usually quiet after eight. And the gym is never busy on Sunday evenings.
Do you have a swimming pool?
Yes. The pool is usually open until ten, but it's always closed on Monday mornings for cleaning.
And how often do the trainers help new members?
They always give you a free plan on your first day, and they often check your progress.
Perfect. I want to start on Wednesday!

questions.q: Ana often gets up before seven.
questions.explain_es: Ana dice: 'I never get up before seven!'

questions.q: When is the gym never busy?
questions.explain_es: Ben dice: 'the gym is never busy on Sunday evenings.'

questions.q: The pool is always closed on Monday mornings.
questions.explain_es: Ben dice: 'it's always closed on Monday mornings for cleaning.'

questions.q: We ____ have three classes every day.
questions.explain_es: 'Usually' significa 'normalmente' y va antes del verbo: 'We usually have three classes every day.'

questions.q: Put the words in order: go / I / dancing / sometimes

questions.explain_es: Ana dice: 'I want to start on Wednesday!'

title: Where Are You Now?

lines.text: Hi, Jack. Where are you? The film starts in ten minutes!
Sorry, Sara! I'm coming. I'm walking to the bus stop now.
The bus stop? Jack! Hurry up!
I'm running now, really. It's raining and I'm getting very wet.
Oh no. Is your brother coming too?
No, he isn't. He's studying for an exam tonight. What are you doing?
I'm standing outside the cinema. I'm holding our tickets.
Is Emma with you?
Yes, she's buying popcorn and drinks right now. People are going inside.
OK, the bus is arriving. I'm getting on now.
Good. We're waiting for you at the door.
I'm coming! See you in five minutes.

title: Welcome to the Beach House
focus: There is / there are + prepositions of place

lines.text: Hello, this is Patricia, the owner of the beach house in Coveñas. Welcome! Here's some information for your stay.
The key is under the green plant pot, next to the front door.
Inside, there's a big living room with a sofa and a TV. There are two bedrooms upstairs.
There are clean towels in the cupboard behind the bathroom door.
In the kitchen, there's a coffee machine on the table, and there are some cups above the sink.
There isn't a washing machine in the house, sorry. But there's a small bakery on the corner, and there's a laundry opposite the bakery.
Outside, there are two bikes behind the house. You can use them.
The beach is very near. It's only five minutes on foot, between the hotel and the fish restaurant.
Are there any problems? Please call me on my mobile. My number is on the fridge.
Have a wonderful holiday. Bye!

title: Join Our Band!

lines.text: Hi, Kevin. Thanks for coming. So, you want to join our band?
Yes, I do. I love music.
Great. What instruments can you play?
I can play the guitar and the piano. I can't play the drums, but I want to learn.
Can you sing?
Yes, I can, but not very well. My sister can sing really well!
Ha! Can you read music?
No, I can't. I play by ear. I listen to a song, and then I can play it.
That's amazing. Can you come to practice on Friday evenings?
Yes, I can. But I can't come on Saturdays because I work.
No problem. We only practise on Fridays. Can you play something for us now?
Sure. Listen to this!

title: How Was Cartagena?
focus: Past simple of be: was / were

lines.text: Hi, Valeria! Where were you last week? You weren't in class.
Hi, Nico! I was in Cartagena with my parents. It was my mum's birthday.
Cool! How was it?
It was wonderful. The weather was hot and sunny every day.
Was your hotel nice?
Yes, it was. It was in the old city, and the rooms were really big.
Were the beaches good?
They were OK, but they were very busy. There were lots of tourists.
And how was the food?
The food was delicious! The fish and the coconut rice were my favourite.
Were you tired after the trip?
Yes, I was very tired, but I was happy. What about you? Were you at home?
Yes, I was. It wasn't very exciting!

questions.q: Who was in Cartagena with Valeria?
questions.explain_es: Valeria dice: 'I was in Cartagena with my parents.'

questions.q: The weather was cold and rainy.
questions.explain_es: Valeria dice: 'The weather was hot and sunny every day.'
Valeria dice: 'It was in the old city.'
Valeria dice: 'they were very busy. There were lots of tourists.'
Con 'you' el pasado de 'be' es 'were': 'Where were you last week?'
Con una cosa (it) usamos 'was': 'The food was delicious!'

questions.q: Find and correct the mistake: 'The rooms was really big.'

title: Fire Drill Instructions

lines.text: Good morning, everyone. This is your head teacher. Today at ten o'clock, we have a fire drill. Please listen carefully.
When you hear the alarm, stop work immediately.
Don't take your bags or your coats. Leave everything in the classroom.
Close the windows, and turn off the lights.
Walk to the door quietly. Don't run, and don't push.
Follow your teacher down the stairs. Don't use the lift.
Go outside to the football field and stand in a line with your class.
Don't talk. Your teacher needs to count the students.
Wait on the football field. Don't go back inside before the second alarm.
Thank you, and remember: stay calm!
